correctness.rationale: A complete analytic argument applies to all a≥0 and K>0. Equal opposite edge currents and strict Hessian positivity force equal acute angles. The remaining balance has two modulo-π branches; any alternative has 1/K≤1, below the global positive branch maximum >1. On the positive branch, derivative factors through one monotone algebraic equation with unique root z>1. The full transverse Hessian has an independent positive mode and a 2×2 determinant equal to 2(g2+g4) times the scalar derivative; this establishes exactly the stable branch and excludes equality. Envelope differentiation proves strict all-weight monotonicity, with separate analytic computations of small-a and infinite-a limits. Finite checks test complete original flow/Hessian at 48 constructed equilibria and critical determinant identities but do not replace universal proof.

value.rationale: The ring is a repeatedly studied natural example of synchronization Braess paradox. Existing studies exhibited the adverse effect numerically and differentiated a different observable. The formula determines the entire sharp stability boundary under edge reinforcement, proves that the paradox never reverses at finite strength, identifies a strictly positive saturation as the strong edge contracts, and computes the first-order onset in a regime where the motivating generic saddle-node theorem fails because of a four-dimensional critical kernel. These are physically and structurally motivated invariants rather than an artificial slice or renamed basic identity.
